reasons: Covers the parser with specific regression cases that match the bugs it was written for.
Does not test rendering, text conversion, or the refusal path in the main routine.

terms.meaning: a test that checks one small piece of code in isolation
a bug that was fixed once and is guarded against coming back
code that reads a command line and turns it into named values
the test tool this project uses to run its test files and report results

used_by: Run by the frontend test command; no caller is visible in the packet.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and the bug it guards
sections.what: Imports the test tool and the argument parser, with a header that names the bug the parser once had.
sections.why: The header records the history: the parser once dropped the view name from the request.
sections.watch_out: The import path depends on the parser's file name, so renaming that file breaks this test.

sections.name: parseArgs
sections.title: Argument parsing checks
sections.what: A group of six checks on the parser: a single view, several views, no arguments, a case with a view, a case alone, and an unknown view name that is kept so the caller can refuse it.
sections.why: Each check matches a specific way the parser could go wrong, and the comments on the first and last explain the particular bugs.
sections.watch_out: The expected values are written by hand, so an intended change to the parser's output shape means editing several checks at once.

summary: Tests the argument parser of the text renderer, checking that view names and case identifiers are read correctly.
purpose: Guards against the earlier bug where a request for one view rendered every view.
why: The comments say that bug also made the unknown-view refusal impossible to trigger in the documented way.
how: Imports the parser and runs it on six argument lists: one view, several views, no arguments, a case with a view, a case alone, and an unknown view name. Each result is compared with the expected value.
inputs: Argument lists written inside the test file.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner. No files are written.
risks: Covers only the parser. Rendering, text conversion and the unknown-view refusal in the main routine are not tested here.
debug: If a test fails, compare the expected value with the value printed in the failure message. A failure in the case-with-view test often means the case value is being taken as a view name. Run this file alone with the frontend test runner to isolate it.
